newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo naphtha firms in line with Europe gains.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo naphtha firms in line with Europe gains.

text.p: Tokyo naphtha prices gained ground for the third successive day on Friday, supported by strength overnight in European markets, traders said.

"There are other reasons for naphtha's rise, such as tight prompt availability after Thailand's spot purchases, but naphtha gains in Europe had by far the largest impact on the Tokyo market today," one trader said.
Open-spec naphtha for second-half September was quoted at around $213.00 a tonne, compared with $210.50 in late Thursday dealing.
Near-term naphtha has seen an upsurge of $13 per tonne in in the last nine business days.
Middle distillate trading remained dull amid high domestic stocks and slack demand.
Gas oil imports, which usually step into full swing in the spring turnaround season, failed to pick up this year due to the high inventories, traders said.
In low sulphur waxy residue (LSWR) trading, talks on August-loading Indonesian cargoes have just started, with few July lots left available in the market, fuel oil traders said.
